question.text: What do traffic signs tell you, and how do they carry meaning?

answer.text: Traffic signs tell you what actions you must take, warn you of possible hazards, and identify routes and locations, and their meaning is carried by color and shape as well as by words, letters, numbers and silhouettes.

teaching.text: Traffic signs tell you what actions you must take, warn you of possible hazards, and identify routes and locations, and their meaning is carried by color and shape as well as by words, letters, numbers and silhouettes. Remember: Act, warn, locate; color and shape. Once more, Act, warn, locate; color and shape.

audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Act, warn, locate; color and shape

question.text: What does the color red on a sign mean?

answer.text: The color red on a sign means an action is prohibited, and red appears on signs of various shapes.

teaching.text: The color red on a sign means an action is prohibited, and red appears on signs of various shapes. This matters because red is the one color that is not tied to a single shape. Remember: Red prohibits, many shapes. Once more, Red prohibits, many shapes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The color red on a sign means an action is prohibited, and red appears on signs of various shapes.

question.text: What do yellow and orange signs mean, and what shapes do they use?

answer.text: Yellow on a sign warns of hazardous or dangerous conditions and almost always appears on a diamond-shaped sign, while orange warns of road work and appears on rectangular or diamond-shaped signs.

teaching.text: Yellow on a sign warns of hazardous or dangerous conditions and almost always appears on a diamond-shaped sign, while orange warns of road work and appears on rectangular or diamond-shaped signs. audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yellow on a sign warns of hazardous or dangerous conditions and almost always appears on a diamond-shaped sign, while orange warns of road work and appears on rectangular or diamond-shaped signs.

question.text: What do black and white signs mean, and which colors mark guide signs?

answer.text: Black and white signs indicate a required action and are always rectangular, while green, blue and brown are used on guide and information signs, mostly rectangular as well.

teaching.text: Black and white signs indicate a required action and are always rectangular, while green, blue and brown are used on guide and information signs, mostly rectangular as well. answer.text: Yellow warns of hazards on a diamond, while orange warns of road work on a diamond or rectangle.

teaching.text: Yellow warns of hazards on a diamond, while orange warns of road work on a diamond or rectangle. Remember: Yellow hazard, orange work. Once more, Yellow hazard, orange work.

question.text: How do black and white signs differ from red signs?

answer.text: Black and white signs command an action and are always rectangular, while red signs prohibit an action and come in various shapes.

teaching.text: Black and white signs command an action and are always rectangular, while red signs prohibit an action and come in various shapes. Remember: Black-white commands, red prohibits. Once more, Black-white commands, red prohibits.

question.text: What is a stop sign, and what must you do at one?

answer.text: A stop sign is an eight-sided white-on-red sign meaning other traffic has the right of way, so you must always come to a complete stop and yield to approaching traffic before proceeding.

teaching.text: A stop sign is an eight-sided white-on-red sign meaning other traffic has the right of way, so you must always come to a complete stop and yield to approaching traffic before proceeding. This matters because the octagon is the only eight-sided sign and is reserved for stop. Remember: Eight sides, always full stop. Once more, Eight sides, always full stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A stop sign is an eight-sided white-on-red sign meaning other traffic has the right of way, so you must always come to a complete stop and yield to approaching traffic before proceeding.

question.text: Where do you stop at a stop sign, and what if you cannot see traffic?

answer.text: At a stop sign you stop at the stop line, or before the marked or unmarked crosswalk if there is no stop line, and if you cannot see traffic from that first stop you move ahead slowly and stop again where you can see approaching traffic.

teaching.text: At a stop sign you stop at the stop line, or before the marked or unmarked crosswalk if there is no stop line, and if you cannot see traffic from that first stop you move ahead slowly and stop again where you can see approaching traffic. Remember: Line or crosswalk, creep, stop again. Once more, Line or crosswalk, creep, stop again.

question.text: What is a yield sign, and when must you stop at one?

answer.text: A yield sign is a triangular red and white sign meaning other traffic has the right of way, so be ready to stop, but you need to stop only when other traffic actually holds the right of way.

teaching.text: A yield sign is a triangular red and white sign meaning other traffic has the right of way, so be ready to stop, but you need to stop only when other traffic actually holds the right of way. Remember: Triangle, stop only when needed. Once more, Triangle, stop only when needed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A yield sign is a triangular red and white sign meaning other traffic has the right of way, so be ready to stop, but you need to stop only when other traffic actually holds the right of way.

question.text: How does a stop sign differ from a yield sign?

answer.text: A stop sign always demands a complete stop, while a yield sign demands a stop only when other traffic holds the right of way.

teaching.text: A stop sign always demands a complete stop, while a yield sign demands a stop only when other traffic holds the right of way. Remember: Stop always, yield when needed. Once more, Stop always, yield when needed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A stop sign always demands a complete stop, while a yield sign demands a stop only when other traffic holds the right of way.

question.text: At a stop sign without a stop line, where do you stop, and when twice?

answer.text: At a stop sign without a stop line you stop before the crosswalk, and when the view is blocked you creep forward and stop a second time where you can see traffic.

teaching.text: At a stop sign without a stop line you stop before the crosswalk, and when the view is blocked you creep forward and stop a second time where you can see traffic. Remember: Crosswalk first, creep, stop again. Once more, Crosswalk first, creep, stop again.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a stop sign without a stop line you stop before the crosswalk, and when the view is blocked you creep forward and stop a second time where you can see traffic.

question.text: What do do not pass signs mark?

answer.text: Do not pass signs are rectangular signs marking places on two- or three-lane roads where you must not pass another vehicle.

teaching.text: Do not pass signs are rectangular signs marking places on two- or three-lane roads where you must not pass another vehicle. Remember: Rectangle, no passing here. Once more, Rectangle, no passing here.

question.text: What is a no passing zone sign, and where is it placed?

answer.text: A no passing zone sign is a pennant-shaped yellow and black sign that supplements the do not pass sign, and it stands on the left side of the road pointing to the start of the no-passing zone.

teaching.text: A no passing zone sign is a pennant-shaped yellow and black sign that supplements the do not pass sign, and it stands on the left side of the road pointing to the start of the no-passing zone. question.text: What does a pass with care sign mark?

answer.text: A pass with care sign is a rectangular black and white sign marking the end of a no-passing zone.

teaching.text: A pass with care sign is a rectangular black and white sign marking the end of a no-passing zone. Remember: Black-white, no-passing zone ends. Once more, Black-white, no-passing zone ends.

question.text: How does a do not pass sign differ from the pennant?

answer.text: A do not pass sign is a rectangle marking the no-passing stretch itself, while the no passing zone pennant on the left merely points to where that stretch begins.

teaching.text: A do not pass sign is a rectangle marking the no-passing stretch itself, while the no passing zone pennant on the left merely points to where that stretch begins. Remember: Sign marks stretch, pennant points. Once more, Sign marks stretch, pennant points.

question.text: How does a pass with care sign differ from a do not pass sign?

answer.text: A pass with care sign ends a no-passing zone, while a do not pass sign begins one.

teaching.text: A pass with care sign ends a no-passing zone, while a do not pass sign begins one. Remember: Care ends, do not begins. Once more, Care ends, do not begins.

question.text: What do speed limit signs show, and what must you obey?

answer.text: Speed limit signs are rectangular black and white signs that show the established maximum and minimum limits, which may apply only at certain times, under certain conditions or to certain kinds of vehicles, and you must drive neither faster than the maximum nor slower than the minimum.

teaching.text: Speed limit signs are rectangular black and white signs that show the established maximum and minimum limits, which may apply only at certain times, under certain conditions or to certain kinds of vehicles, and you must drive neither faster than the maximum nor slower than the minimum. question.text: What does a reduced speed ahead sign tell you?

answer.text: A reduced speed ahead sign has the same color and shape as a speed limit sign and gives advance notice to begin slowing, and the new lower limit takes effect at the next speed limit sign.

teaching.text: A reduced speed ahead sign has the same color and shape as a speed limit sign and gives advance notice to begin slowing, and the new lower limit takes effect at the next speed limit sign. answer.text: Exclusion signs are rectangular and show either a red circle on white or a red circle with a red diagonal slash on black and white, and they restrict or prohibit vehicles, vehicle movements or other activities.

question.text: Why are devices used in work zones, and what is their basic color?

answer.text: Construction and maintenance work areas use traffic control devices to guide drivers and pedestrians safely through the work zone and to protect highway workers, and orange is the basic color of these devices.

answer.text: The diagonal stripes on a barricade or vertical panel point the way traffic should pass, with stripes sloping down to the right meaning bear right and stripes sloping down to the left meaning bear left.
